root_cause.text: The x86 CR4 pinning logic incorrectly treated X86_CR4_FRED as a permanently pinned post-init bit even though FRED is enabled before its per-CPU MSRs are fully initialized on BSP/AP boot paths, creating an unsafe window that led to a later workaround of disabling CR4 pinning based on a writable online flag.
root_cause.evidence: The patch removes `X86_CR4_FRED` from `cr4_pinned_mask` in `arch/x86/kernel/cpu/common.c`, and the CVE/commit message explicitly states that FRED is initialized “first on the BSP and later on the APs,” leaving “a window in time when exceptions cannot be handled,” and that temporarily disabling CR4 pinning for not-yet-online APs was insecure because “an attack on the kernel needs to only modify the online bit ... and then disable CR4 pinning and then disable SM*P.”

vuln_statements.content: static const unsigned long cr4_pinned_mask = X86_CR4_SMEP | X86_CR4_SMAP | X86_CR4_UMIP |

agent_logs.evidence_points: The patch removes `X86_CR4_FRED` from `cr4_pinned_mask` in `arch/x86/kernel/cpu/common.c`, and the CVE/commit message explicitly states that FRED is initialized “first on the BSP and later on the APs,” leaving “a window in time when exceptions cannot be handled,” and that temporarily disabling CR4 pinning for not-yet-online APs was insecure because “an attack on the kernel needs to only modify the online bit ... and then disable CR4 pinning and then disable SM*P.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Stop pinning the CR4 FRED bit after CPU initialization so it can be changed at runtime when needed.
intent_record.what: The constant initializer for `cr4_pinned_mask` was changed to remove `X86_CR4_FRED` from the bitwise-OR list, leaving `X86_CR4_SMEP | X86_CR4_SMAP | X86_CR4_UMIP | X86_CR4_FSGSBASE | X86_CR4_CET` as the pinned CR4 bits.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the CR4 pinning mechanism will no longer treat the FRED control bit as immutable after CPU initialization, allowing that CR4 bit to change later instead of being enforced as pinned like the remaining listed features.

grouping_result.intent: Stop pinning the CR4 FRED bit after CPU initialization so it can be changed at runtime when needed.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly targets the root cause by removing post-init pinning of X86_CR4_FRED, which was incorrectly treated as permanently pinned and created the unsafe initialization window.
